Your parents may mean well, but it's essential to respect your boundaries and not force you to participate in events that make you uncomfortable. It's not about being rude or unkind; it's about taking care of yourself and your mental well-being. In this scenario, you've already expressed your discomfort and disinterest in attending the wedding multiple times, and it's not unreasonable to expect your parents to respect your wishes. Being "dragged" to the wedding against your will can be stressful and anxiety-provoking, and it's not fair to expect you to pretend to be enthusiastic or sociable when you're not feeling it. It's okay to prioritize your own needs and set boundaries with your family. You can still maintain a relationship with them without feeling obligated to attend every social event or gathering. It might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with your parents about your boundaries and needs, and work together to find a compromise that respects your comfort level.
